newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power prices hold after holiday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power prices hold after holiday.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. were steady Friday as most traders had already scheduled electricity deliveries through the long holiday weekend, industry sources said.
Firm, peak power in the northern part of Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Monday delivery was notionally in the $21.00-23.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, unchanged from Wednesday.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was notionally assessed around $15.50, which is mostly unchanged.

At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Monday delivery were around $24.50 per MWh, as compared to Wednesday's trading range for Friday delivery at $22.00.
Firm, off-peak power for the weekend at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally assessed in the $16.00-17.00 range.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to be slightly above-normal this weekend, with colder air moving in on Monday and Tuesday. The six- to 10-day outlook shows mostly normal temperatures.
Separately, Entergy Corp's 1,173 megawatt (MW) Grand Gulf 1 nuclear unit in Port Gibson, Miss., is in start-up mode, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission reported.
Also, Tennessee Valley Authority's 1,170 MW Watts Bar nuclear power plant was reduced to 50 percent power due to leaking condensor tubes.
